patch.value: pm-rl: an RL programme as tracked project data

An RL programme is one of the most context-heavy things an agent can run, and today its context lives in a dashboard, a folder of JSON and shell history: not reviewable, not merge-safe, and not available to the agent deciding what to train next. pm-rl makes the programme itself a tracker. Two pm properties do the real work. Metric logging is append-only and so is pm history, which unions losslessly under concurrent writers on separate branches, so two agents sweeping on two branches never lose rows. And runs form a dependency graph pm already models and queries, so the question that actually costs teams weeks - which results does this reward-spec change invalidate - is a reachability query rather than a feature.

Every item type registers with typed fields under the host schema; a run's metric series is only ever written to history; two concurrent runs on two branches merge to the union of both series against real git branches; leaderboard and invalidate answer from the dependency graph; 100 percent line, branch, function and docstring coverage

value.text:
Re-verified this session (pi-agent). Every acceptance criterion in THIS epic is satisfied against the current tree: all nine item types register with typed fields under the host schema; a run's metric series is only ever written to history (never a body); two concurrent writers on two real git branches merge to the union of both series — proven for plain runs and again for independent sweep arms; leaderboard and invalidate answer from the stored dependency graph; npm run coverage reports 17 source file(s) at 100/100/100 lines/branches/functions and npm run docstring reports 17 file(s), 123 declaration(s) documented, with release:check fully green.

The epic stays BLOCKED for exactly one reason, inherited from its child pm-rl-et5b: host-level write-time interception of arbitrary core mutations (see that item's re-verification note — pm-cli#854 closed without delivering an extension-registerable mutation-invariant hook in 2026.8.20). Nothing else is missing; if et5b unblocks or the fleet agrees use-time detection satisfies its intent, this epic can close immediately on the evidence above.
